name: Cytoskeleton
short_description: Scaffold, muscle and railway in one, built from three kinds of fibre: thin actin filaments shape the cell surface and let cells crawl, medium intermediate filaments provide tensile strength, and thick microtubules act as transport rails and pull the chromosomes apart during division.

textbook.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; good centrosome-radiating composition and a genuinely hollow-tipped microtubule, but the teal INTERMEDIATE FILAMENT rope was drawn visibly THICKER than the blue MICROTUBULE tubes — a direct violation of the thin-actin < medium-intermediate < thick-microtubule ordering that is the whole teaching point of this subject — and the motor protein was rendered as a literal human mannequin figure walking a tightrope with a ball on a string, an anthropomorphised design not permitted in the scientific plates. Fix-prompt: state the exact thickness ordering numerically (intermediate filament roughly half the microtubule's diameter), and replace the motor protein description with an explicit non-human two-lobed molecular blob with leg-like appendages, no head/face/arms/torso)
textbook.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; fix applied cleanly — verified by direct pixel comparison that the teal intermediate-filament braid is now clearly and consistently thinner than the blue microtubule tubes, which are themselves unmistakably the thickest fibre with a visible open hollow bore at multiple tube ends and a finely ridged surface; the coral-red microfilament mesh remains the thinnest of the three. The motor protein is now a non-human two-lobed amber-gold blob with curled leg-like appendages gripping a microtubule, towing a separate pale vesicle on a thread — verified on a magnified crop, no human anatomy, no face. Microtubules radiate correctly from a centrosome hub. No baked-in text anywhere (checked on a magnified crop of the motor-protein region). Used as the primary labelled figure (svg_theme)

sem.1: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image, accepted on the first attempt; a convincing false-colour SEM of an 'unroofed cell' fibre meshwork — a fine coral-red actin mesh fills the whole background (thinnest), teal-green intermediate filaments form a visibly thinner-than-microtubule tangle at the hub and along the radiating fibres, and thick mid-blue microtubules radiate outward from the centre with an unmistakable round HOLLOW bore at the very centre of the hub (verified on a magnified crop) — the relative thickness ordering reads correctly at a glance. A tiny amber two-lobed motor-protein particle with curled leg-like appendages (non-human, verified on a magnified crop) grips one microtubule. No baked-in text, scale bar or watermark anywhere in the frame. Not labelled, per project convention that the SEM plate is the surface plate rather than a labelled diagram)

3d.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; good full-bleed composition, translucent membrane with actin cortex, correctly thin-vs-thick fibre ordering already mostly reasonable, but the motor protein was again rendered as a small human/humanoid mannequin figure with a string-and-ball tightrope-walking pose — an anthropomorphised design not permitted. Fix-prompt: same non-human two-lobed molecular-blob motor-protein description as the textbook fix, and reiterate 'must never resemble a person')
3d.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; motor protein is now a non-human amber-gold two-lobed blob with curled leg-like appendages on a microtubule, towing a translucent pale vesicle sphere — verified on a magnified crop, no human anatomy. Thickness ordering verified correct: thin coral-red actin mesh along the cortex, clearly thinner teal-green intermediate filament ropes, and clearly thickest mid-blue microtubules with several visible open hollow bores at cut ends (verified on a magnified crop), radiating from a centrosome hub beside a glowing nucleus sphere. Natural biological tones throughout, not neon, not monochrome. Full bleed to all four edges, no border/frame/vignette. No baked-in text anywhere. Used as a labelled figure)

watercolor.1: fail (gemini-2.5-flash-image; correct hollow-microtubule rendering with a visible bore, but the composition left large plain-paper margins on the right and bottom — a 'sheet on the page' look rather than full bleed — and the coral-red microfilaments and teal-green intermediate filaments read as very similar thickness/twist pattern, undermining the size-ordering point; the motor protein was again a literal human figure. Fix-prompt: explicitly require the fibre bundle and membrane arc to bleed off all four edges filling at least ~92% of the frame, sharpen the microfilament-vs-intermediate-filament thickness contrast, and apply the same non-human motor-protein description)
watercolor.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; full bleed achieved — fibres, membrane arc and vesicles cross all four edges of the frame with only small slivers of aged paper visible between them (verified by inspecting all four edges directly), no mat/frame/border/drop-shadow. Thickness ordering verified correct: fine coral-red microfilament threads clearly thinner than the teal-green braided intermediate-filament rope, which is in turn clearly thinner than the bold mid-blue microtubule tubes, two of which show a clearly painted open hollow bore with fine hatching suggesting the ridged tubulin lattice (verified on a magnified crop). Motor protein is a non-human two-lobed amber blob with curled ink-stroke legs, towing a pale vesicle on a fine ink thread — no human anatomy. No baked-in text anywhere. One honestly-noted stray unlabelled brownish blob near the nucleus wash reads as an ambiguous extra shape not called for in the prompt or the reference list; it is not mistakeable for DNA/chromatin or any forbidden structure and was left alone rather than spending a further paid attempt chasing a cosmetic-only imperfection. Used as a labelled figure)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons 'FluorescentCells.jpg', an ImageJ sample image and a work of the US Federal Government — PUBLIC DOMAIN. A genuine immunofluorescence LIGHT micrograph, not an electron micrograph, of bovine pulmonary artery endothelial cells: nuclei stained blue with DAPI, microtubules green with a Bodipy FL antibody against tubulin, and F-actin red with Texas Red-X phalloidin. Viewed directly and confirmed to show all three: blue nuclei, a green microtubule network filling the cytoplasm, and a red cortical actin mesh concentrated at the cell margins. Colours are fluorescent stains, not a natural property. Intermediate filaments and motor proteins are NOT visible in this plate and rest on the illustrated styles and the literature instead. Native 512x512, upscaled ~2.1x to 1080x1080 by fetch_reference.py — stated rather than implied. No baked-in text or scale bar, so edit_image.py was skipped entirely. REPLACES the earlier NIGMS 'Colorful cells' plate (Torsten Wittmann, entry 2428), which was CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 — the only NonCommercial image among more than a hundred references here. Its NC term would have propagated to anyone reusing the collection, so it was swapped for a freely reusable equivalent rather than kept for its slightly higher resolution.
decision: use as final and as the primary labelled figure; attempt 1 on gemini-2.5-flash-image drew the intermediate filament thicker than the microtubule and anthropomorphised the motor protein as a human mannequin; attempt 2 fixed both with an explicit numeric thickness ordering and a non-human two-lobed motor-protein description, passed clean on the same model, no escalation needed
